PAY ATTENTION / FIELD NOTES EDITION 01 · 10 SEPTEMBER 2026
SIX FINDINGS.
ONE LIFE.

THE INDIAN
ATTENTION
REPORT.

Work, screens and the life in between.

A desk-researched first edition for curious people. Indian and urban findings, plus one global workplace comparison. No original survey or diary study has been conducted.

Follow the numbers ↓
TIME SPENT ≠ ATTENTION GIVEN
01 / WORK URBAN INDIA · 2024

The day has
a day job.

490MIN / DAY

Average employment-related time among urban participants aged 6+ who did that activity on the surveyed day.

Work gets the first claim on the day.

A question for you

When work ends, what do you want to have energy left for?

Read the evidence

MoSPI Time Use Survey 2024, Table 2; released February 2025. Participant average, not a metro-professional benchmark. 490 minutes = 8 hours 10 minutes.

Open official source ↗
02 / LEISURE URBAN INDIA · 2024

Life beyond
the to-do list.

183MIN / DAY

Average time in culture, leisure, mass media and sport among urban participants aged 6+ taking part that day.

Three hours of “leisure” can mean very different things.

A question for you

Which part of yesterday would you happily repeat?

Read the evidence

MoSPI TUS 2024, Table 2. No screen-time split. Different participant base from finding 01; do not combine these means into one person’s day.

Open official source ↗
03 / CARE ALL INDIA · 2024

Someone needs
you, too.

Women 140 min
Men 74 min

Daily unpaid household caregiving time among participants aged 15 to 59. National figures, including rural and urban India.

A day is not always yours alone.

A question for you

Who makes room in their day so that you can have room in yours?

Read the evidence

MoSPI TUS 2024, key highlights. Rounded participant means; not all adults, solely employed people, or total unpaid work.

Open official source ↗
04 / VIDEO INDIAN VIDEO AUDIENCE · 2026

Just one
more?

14.9HOURS / WEEK

Ormax’s estimate of average weekly online-video viewing per member of India’s online-video audience.

The number tells us how long.
Not whether any of it stayed.

A question for you

What did you watch recently that stayed with you? What didn’t?

Read the evidence

Ormax OTT Audience Report 2026, publisher summary dated 10 September 2026. Fieldwork: June to July 2026; 15,000 respondents across India. Audience means anyone watching free or paid online video in the previous month. Includes social video, micro dramas and FAST channels. Full questionnaire and weighting were not inspected; treat this as an attributed publisher estimate, not a target-group benchmark.

Open publisher source ↗
05 / WORKPLACE PINGS GLOBAL COMPARISON · 2025

Read the
small print.

2MIN BETWEEN PINGS*

*For the top 20% of Microsoft 365 users by ping volume, during core work hours. Not the average Indian professional.

Before you panic: read the asterisk.

A question for you

Which interruptions deserve your attention, and which could wait?

Read the evidence

Microsoft, Breaking down the infinite workday, 17 June 2025. Aggregated telemetry ending 15 February 2025; education and EU tenants excluded. Pings include meeting invites, emails and chats, not observed mental switches. The related 275-pings figure spans 24 hours; it is not an eight-hour count. This finding is international context.

Open source and methodology ↗
06 / PEOPLE & NUMBERS INDIA · OCTOBER 2025

A person is
more than a user.

500MILLION USER IDENTITIES

DataReportal’s estimate of active social-media user identities in India. These are not necessarily unique people.

Half a billion identities.
Not half a billion individual people.

A question for you

Where online do you feel most like yourself?

Read the evidence

Digital 2026: India, published in late 2025. This figure describes October 2025, not a 2026 survey. User identities, platform ad reach and time spent are different measures. Do not add audiences across platforms or convert reach into attention share.

Open source and definitions ↗
THE QUESTION THE NUMBERS CAN’T ANSWER FOR YOU.
I know where my time went.
Is that where I wanted
my life to go?

These questions do not collect responses.

About this edition · sources, boundaries and corrections

Edition 01, published 10 September 2026. Sources were checked on that date. Observation years appear on each finding. Findings 01 to 03 share one survey and are not independent evidence. Findings 04 to 06 use different populations and methods; they cannot be combined into a single attention budget. Human implications and reflection questions are our editorial interpretation, not additional research findings.

The report measures aspects of time use and digital activity, not a universal attention span. No original participant accounts, representative metro survey or causal conclusions are presented. The photographs elsewhere on this site are generated illustrations, not research records. Report corrections will be documented with a date and explanation here.

Edition history: 10 September 2026 · first desk-researched edition; six findings published. No corrections recorded.

Notes & sources

The colour exercise is inspired by the Stroop task. The exception exercise is inspired by the Sustained Attention to Response Task. These shortened adaptations are not validated assessments. Search rounds differ in layout and order and cannot isolate the effect of distraction. The opening exercise involves both attention and memory. No population rankings or diagnostic scores are calculated.
